steps.reason: 52 rows are exact copies of another row in all 15 columns. Because fnlwgt (the census weight, 28,523 distinct values) is one of them, such a row is almost certainly a copy and not two people who happen to share every attribute. Removing them before fnlwgt is dropped keeps train and test free of repeated records.
fnlwgt is the census sampling weight, a property of the survey and not of the person. education repeats education-num one to one, so the numeric version is kept.
Stratified: 24% of the people earn more than 50K.
These columns are missing for 2% to 6% of the people and the missingness is itself informative (unknown workclass and occupation go together), so it becomes its own category.
Text categories with up to 14 values; one-hot is the family-neutral encoding.
41 countries, 90% of them the United States; rare countries are grouped to avoid dozens of near-empty columns.

Numeric columns are on very different scales (capital-gain reaches the tens of thousands). The model family is open and may include linear models; scaling costs trees nothing and puts linear models on comparable footing.
